question: In March 2023, EIOPA completed a report on Euroins Romania, part of the Euroins Insurance Group, a major insurance group operating throughout central, eastern and south-eastern Europe. This report has not been made available to Members of the European Parliament. Remarkably, the Commission recently admitted that it has not had access to the report either.

The Regulation establishing EIOPA1 provides that EIOPA is accountable to Parliament. However, Parliament cannot fulfill its responsibilities regarding EIOPA while being denied access to a report prepared by EIOPA on a case that has had significant economic and social impacts in parts of the EU.

In the interest of openness and transparency, will the Commission carry out a full review of the EIOPA report, the conclusions it reached and the source of the data used in its preparation, and will it make this review and its findings available to Parliament?

Regulation (EU) No 1094/2010 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 November 2010 establishing a European Supervisory Authority (European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority), amending Decision No 716/2009/EC and repealing Commission Decision 2009/79/EC (OJ L 331, 15.12.2010, p. 48).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.3.2024) The Commission understands that the report by the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA), which the Honourable Member refers to, was adopted pursuant to Article 8(1), point (b) of Regulation (EU) No 1094/2010 (EIOPA Regulation)1 with a view to assessing the correct and consistent application of the Solvency II framework2.

This report, which contains confidential prudential information, has not been made public, nor has it been shared with the Commission. The Honourable Member may, however, wish to submit a request for access to documents to EIOPA directly.

In addition, pursuant to Article 3 of the EIOPA Regulation3, the Chairperson of EIOPA may be requested to hold confidential oral discussions with relevant participants of the competent committee of the European Parliament. The Commission has not received any evidence of irregularities related to the preparation or content of EIOPA’s report.
Finally, the Commission understands that the Euroins Insurance Group is currently challenging EIOPA’s report at the Court of Justice of the European Union (see cases T416/23 and T-586/23).
1 OJ L 331, 15.12.2010, p. 48–83. 2 https://www.eiopa.europa.eu/browse/regulation-and-policy/solvency-ii_en 3 OJ L 331, 15.12.2010, p. 48–83.
